evals.prompt: I'm taking over a 3-year-old Flask project and I'd like a full health check before I start refactoring. The code lives in ./backend. Tell me where the technical debt is.
evals.expected_output: A file python_health_report.md at the root of ./backend containing the YAML header and the 5 top-level sections (2.1/2.2 are subsections of section 2), with a justified A-F grade, and exactly 3 concrete actions in the action plan. The tools Ruff, Vulture, Radon and Pylint must all have been invoked.
expectations: The file python_health_report.md exists at the root of the audited project
A YAML header with audit.grade and metrics (ruff, vulture, avg_mi, sloc) is present at the top of the report
All 5 top-level sections (Executive Summary, Dead Code, Complexity, Duplication, Action Plan) are present
No source .py file has been modified (read-only) and no cache directory (e.g. .ruff_cache) was created
The commands ruff, vulture, radon cc, radon mi, radon raw and pylint have all been executed
An A-F grade appears in the Executive Summary and in the YAML header
The action plan contains exactly 3 numbered actions
No ruff --fix or automatic fix has been applied
The Vulture false-positive warning is present

evals.prompt: On my project . I think I've copy-pasted a lot of CSV parsing blocks across my services. Can you check duplication and, while you're at it, tell me if I have functions I no longer use?
evals.expected_output: Report generated, with section 4 (Duplication) populated if pylint actually detects duplicates, and section 2 (Ruff + Vulture Dead Code) documented.
expectations: The file python_health_report.md is created
Section 4 Code Duplication is present even if empty (with explicit mention 'No duplication detected')
Both subsections 2.1 Ruff and 2.2 Vulture are present
The Vulture false-positive warning is present
No source file modified

evals.prompt: Je reprends un vieux projet Django. Tu peux me faire un bilan de santé complet avant que je commence la refonte ? Le code est dans ./backend. Dis-moi où est la dette technique.
evals.expected_output: Same behavior as eval 1 (French prompt): python_health_report.md at the root of ./backend with YAML header, 5 sections, justified A-F grade, exactly 3 actions, all 4 tools invoked.
expectations: The file python_health_report.md exists at the root of the audited project
The audit tools were run against ./backend (not the repository root)
A YAML header with audit.grade is present
All 5 top-level sections are present
An A-F grade appears in the Executive Summary
The action plan contains exactly 3 numbered actions
No source file modified

evals.prompt: Run an extended health audit on this project: the usual dead code and complexity check, plus my dependencies for known vulnerabilities and my docstring coverage.
evals.expected_output: Standard report plus section 6 (Extended Findings) with 6.1 Dependencies (pip-audit result or explicit skip reason), 6.2 Docstring coverage (interrogate), 6.3 TODO/FIXME census, 6.4 Git churn. The grade is computed on core metrics only.
expectations: The file python_health_report.md is created with the 5 core sections
Section 6 Extended Findings is present with the 4 subsections
pip-audit was invoked OR an explicit skip reason is stated (no requirements file / network error)
interrogate was invoked and reports a docstring coverage percentage
The grade is derived from core metrics only (section 6 does not affect it)
No source file modified

evals.prompt: Re-run the health audit — I cleaned up some things since the last report.
evals.expected_output: A previous python_health_report.md exists (v2 format with YAML header). The new report contains a 'Since last audit' line in the Executive Summary, metric deltas, and a history array carried forward and appended in the YAML header.
expectations: The previous report was read before being overwritten
The Executive Summary contains a 'Since last audit (<date>)' line with the previous grade and the new grade
The YAML header contains a history array including at least the previous audit date+grade and the new one
The previous report's metrics are not lost (history carried forward)
No source file modified
